name: Glass atrium (玻璃中庭温室)
notes: Origin: the gallery floor directly below the painting's viewpoint; +Y runs across the gallery towards the far curtain wall, +X along it, Z up; metres.

Gallery: a glass floor (top at z = 0) on polished jade beams over the garden, south of y = 4.18 and on the west wing; the stairwell (x -5.0..-2.16, y -1.6..4.18) and the atrium north of the edge are open.  The edge is guarded by a frameless glass balustrade whose top edge carries short jade stanchions between two rails (0.91 and 1.04 m) -- the painting draws the stanchions only between the rails.

Through the atrium the view falls on the paved north end of the garden (1 m flags: their joints are the regular lines behind the railing) and, through the lower curtain wall, on the pink haze outside.

Garden: planted cell by cell from a planting plan read off the painting (calibration/planting_plan.py -> data/planting.json): where the painting shows foliage up to a height above a cell, the cell carries plants that tall (ground cover, understory or shrubs); where it shows the pale floor it stays paved; cells seen only through glassware take their neighbours' class; cells the painting's camera cannot see are planted by design -- except the foot of the stair, the court along the north wall and the floor under the garden furniture.

Stair (dog-leg, glass treads): 14 treads (0.12308 m risers, 0.433 m goings) along x = -4.62..-3.12 rise from the garden at y = 0.32 to a landing at z = -1.354, then 11 treads turn west up to the gallery floor at x = -9.383; solved from the painted nosings (16 px rms).

Envelope: curtain walls on a 2 m module at x = -12.46 / 13.54 and y = -6 / 16, a glazed roof at z = 7.22; the conservatory crowns a 117 m tower: the frame's top row of image looks 6 degrees below the horizon, so the pink seen through the walls is the sunlit city haze far below, not sky.  North of the tower a podium rises to 16 m below the garden, reaching 33 m out -- just short of where its roof would rise above the sight line past the foot of the north wall, so the roof itself is never seen and the view beyond it falls into the haze; the trees on its roof terrace, 30-45 m away, are the pale canopies seen through the north wall down to its foot (their tops placed on the painted canopy outline, their trunks and the terrace below every sight line through the wall), veiled by the haze between.  The faint tree further off stands on a lower roof 84 m north (a crown 6.3 m wide, sized on its painted silhouette); that roof, too, ends before it would rise above the sight line past the wall foot.

Garden specimens ("Painted ..."): each placed where its mass is in the painting -- the centre pixel of the mass back-projected through the solved camera at the height of its crown; the random understory fills the beds between them.

Air: the sunlit air fills the conservatory 10 cm clear of the floor and roof -- a volume boundary must not coincide with another volume boundary (the glass posts end on those planes), or the volume stack at the camera breaks and every camera ray is absorbed.

Side table: the painting draws its top as an ellipse rounder (aspect 0.57) than a horizontal disc can project to at that place (every point on that view ray gives sin 26 deg = 0.44); the disc matches the painted width and centre, the objects on it their painted corners.

Sun: 55 deg high from azimuth 30 deg (to the right of and behind the atrium), so its shafts run down and to the left through the air as the painted ones do.  It shines through the city smog, which scatters the blue out of it: golden light (1.0, 0.9, 0.45) -- the painted sun patches on the pale pink floor are orange-yellow, not pink-white.

Shade trees: three umbrella trees in the unseen north-east of the garden (outside the painting frame) whose crowns stand between the sun and the paved court: their dappled shade is the green-and-pink mottling of the court floor seen through the balustrade, and the sun shafts come down between their leaves.

North wall: structurally glazed -- its panes meet on silicone joints, so only the transoms and the corner mullions are frames (the painting shows the pink haze through it undivided but for two horizontal bars).  Posts that the painting shows only below the gallery floor stop under it.

Daylight: the sky's strength is 0.26 of the sun's power (sky.sun_ratio): a hazy sky giving some 40 % of the light on a level surface with the sun 55 degrees up (pi * 0.26 * 0.7 against sin 55, for a dome averaging 0.7 of its strength); the fit scales both together.

Vines: climbing plants trained along the roof frame, 6.3-6.6 m above the gallery, above every sight line of the painting's camera: they are seen only in their dappled shade -- the leaf-shaped sun patches on the court, the treads and the gallery -- and in the shafts of sun between them.  The sun is the real sun, half a degree across, so the patches keep sharp edges from nine metres up.

City extent: the city ground and the haze reach 6 km out: the top row of the frame looks 6 degrees down, so its sight line meets the ground 1.2 km away -- inside the haze, where the ground has no edge to show.
